description: Detector-framework fixture shared by both runtimes. Pins what is deterministic: the registered detector descriptors, denominator derivation from patient-level records, and the observed/expected/log-likelihood of the top cluster from a fixed case-event series. It does NOT pin p-values or recurrence intervals: the desktop seeds an FNV-1a/xorshift stream and the server a SHA-256-seeded random.Random, so Monte Carlo results differ by simulation noise on identical input. Pinning them would tie the two generators together, which is a stronger promise than either product needs.

detectors.name: Space-time permutation scan
detectors.blindSpot: Conditions on the location and time margins, so a rise that is uniform across every location leaves no interaction to find. The all-location category scan covers part of that case and not all of it.
detectors.citation: Kulldorff M, et al. A Space-Time Permutation Scan Statistic for Disease Outbreak Detection. PLOS Medicine 2005;2:e59. doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.0020059

detectors.method: Kulldorff Bernoulli scan statistic on resistant-among-tested
detectors.citation: Kulldorff M. A spatial scan statistic. Communications in Statistics: Theory and Methods 1997;26:1481-1496. doi:10.1080/03610929708831995
detectors.name: Bernoulli proportion scan, space-time
detectors.blindSpot: Sees the resistant share and not the count, so an outbreak that doubles the number of resistant isolates while testing doubles alongside it is invisible here and visible to the case-only permutation scan. The two are complementary, which is why Phase 31 runs both.

detectors.method: Kulldorff Bernoulli scan statistic on resistant-among-tested
detectors.citation: Kulldorff M. A spatial scan statistic. Communications in Statistics: Theory and Methods 1997;26:1481-1496. doi:10.1080/03610929708831995
detectors.name: Bernoulli proportion scan, purely temporal
detectors.blindSpot: Collapses location, so a rise confined to one ward is diluted by every other ward and may not reach significance. It is the scan for a deployment that has one location, not a substitute for the space-time scan in one that has several.

detectors.method: Kulldorff Bernoulli scan statistic on resistant-among-tested
detectors.citation: Kulldorff M. A spatial scan statistic. Communications in Statistics: Theory and Methods 1997;26:1481-1496. doi:10.1080/03610929708831995
detectors.name: Bernoulli proportion scan, purely spatial
detectors.blindSpot: Collapses time, so a ward whose resistance rose sharply last month and was ordinary for the eleven before it is averaged back to ordinary. It ranks standing burden, not change.

detectors.method: Kulldorff Poisson scan statistic on cases per population at risk
detectors.citation: Kulldorff M. A spatial scan statistic. Communications in Statistics: Theory and Methods 1997;26:1481-1496. doi:10.1080/03610929708831995
detectors.name: Poisson rate scan, space-time
detectors.blindSpot: Trusts the population series it is given. If a ward closes to admissions because of the outbreak, its patient-days fall, the expected count falls with them, and the excess is inflated by the response rather than the event. The Bernoulli model does not have this failure, and has others.

detectors.method: Kulldorff Poisson scan statistic on cases per population at risk
detectors.citation: Kulldorff M. A spatial scan statistic. Communications in Statistics: Theory and Methods 1997;26:1481-1496. doi:10.1080/03610929708831995
detectors.name: Poisson rate scan, purely temporal
detectors.blindSpot: Collapses location, so a rise confined to one ward is diluted by every other. It also inherits the Poisson failure: a population series that responds to the outbreak moves the expectation in the same direction as the excess.

detectors.name: Multivariate proportion scan
detectors.method: Kulldorff multivariate scan statistic over Bernoulli streams, isolate-permutation null
detectors.blindSpot: Combines the agents of one organism, so an outbreak of a single-agent phenotype gains nothing here and pays the multiplicity of every other agent in the panel. It also inherits the Bernoulli blind spot: it sees the resistant share, not the count.
detectors.citation: Kulldorff M, Mostashari F, Duczmal L, Yih WK, Kleinman K, Platt R. Multivariate scan statistics for disease surveillance. Statistics in Medicine 2007;26:1824-1833. doi:10.1002/sim.2818

detectors.name: EWMA control chart
detectors.method: Exponentially weighted moving average on period counts
detectors.blindSpot: Has no spatial dimension: a cluster spread over two wards is two half-strength series and may cross no limit, where a scan statistic pools them. The smoothing that makes it stable also damps a single very large period, and it corrects for no multiplicity at all.
detectors.citation: Roberts SW. Control chart tests based on geometric moving averages. Technometrics 1959;1:239-250. doi:10.1080/00401706.1959.10489860

detectors.name: Poisson CUSUM
detectors.method: Page cumulative sum on period counts, Lucas Poisson reference value
detectors.blindSpot: Says the process has shifted, not when: the accumulated sum carries no information about where in the run the change began, so the reported window is the run above the limit and not the outbreak. Counts only, so a rise in testing volume reads as a rise in resistance.
detectors.citation: Page ES. Continuous inspection schemes. Biometrika 1954;41:100-115. doi:10.2307/2333009; Lucas JM. Counted data CUSUMs. Technometrics 1985;27:129-144. doi:10.1080/00401706.1985.10488030

detectors.name: Bernoulli CUSUM on the resistant proportion
detectors.method: Reynolds-Stoumbos Bernoulli cumulative sum on resistant-among-tested
detectors.blindSpot: Inherits every CUSUM limitation — no spatial pooling, no multiplicity correction, no statement of when the shift began — and adds a dependence on the baseline proportion being stable. A laboratory that changed its testing panel mid-series has changed p0 underneath the chart, and the chart cannot tell that from a change in resistance.
detectors.citation: Reynolds MR, Stoumbos ZG. A general approach to modeling CUSUM charts for a proportion. IIE Transactions 2000;32:515-535. doi:10.1080/07408170008963928

detectors.name: Farrington aberration detection
detectors.method: Farrington 1996 quasi-Poisson regression on seasonal reference periods
detectors.blindSpot: Needs years of history: with five reference years no period inside the first five years can be tested at all, and no corpus this repository generates is that long. Purely temporal, so a cluster split across two wards is two half-strength series. And its reweighting suppresses a sustained rise as readily as a past outbreak, so creeping resistance is absorbed into the baseline rather than detected.
detectors.citation: Farrington CP, Andrews NJ, Beale AD, Catchpole MA. A statistical algorithm for the early detection of outbreaks of infectious disease. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society A 1996;159:547-563. doi:10.2307/2983331

detectors.name: Bayesian spatial scan
detectors.method: Neill Gamma-Poisson Bayesian spatial scan statistic
detectors.blindSpot: Its answer moves with a prior the data does not set, and unlike a p-value there is no convention to fall back on. It uses the same margin-conditioned baseline as the permutation scan and so inherits that blind spot: a rise uniform across every location is absorbed into the time margin. And the posterior is conditional on the outbreak being one of the regions enumerated, so it ranks the best of a bad set with the same confidence as a good one.
detectors.citation: Neill DB, Moore AW, Cooper GF. A Bayesian spatial scan statistic. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 2005;18:1003-1010.

detectors.name: PACE (phenotype-aggregated cluster evaluation)
detectors.method: Phenotype-aggregated dual-model scan: Kulldorff space-time permutation and Bernoulli proportion scans over mechanism-level streams, combined by Šidák correction
detectors.blindSpot: Pools agents by the catalogue's mechanism class, so it mis-pools wherever that class does not match the mechanism for an organism — carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa is often porin loss rather than a transmissible carbapenemase. It also inherits both parents' limits: a rise uniform across every ward leaves the case-only arm nothing to find, and the proportion arm cannot see an outbreak whose testing volume rose with it.

denominators.note: An agent counts as tested when the record carries R, I or S for it. I is not counted as resistant: the scan refuses to merge it, so counting it here would make numerator and denominator disagree about what resistance means. The empty-string antibiotic_code row is the organism-level isolate count.

runtime_labels.note: The two runtimes scan different islands, so the all-island cluster is named differently and correctly in each. The desktop scans wards inside one laboratory and calls the aggregate "All locations"; the portal scans reporting sites across a federation and calls it "All sites". The statistic is identical -- the log-likelihood ratios below agree to three decimals across runtimes -- so a parity test must compare the numbers and map this label, not demand one product use the other product's word for a thing it does not have.

scan.note: Settings use 99 permutations so the fixture runs fast. That caps the reachable recurrence interval at 100 days, which is why recurrenceThresholdDays is 50 here and not the shipped 365.

bernoulli.note: Deterministic geometry only. p-values are not pinned: the two runtimes seed different generators, so Monte Carlo p-values differ by simulation noise on identical input. What is pinned is the cluster each shape finds and the log-likelihood ratio it assigns.

poisson.note: The population series is supplied, never derived: no laboratory record carries a population at risk. Medical ICU holds 40% of the patient-days and, in the last four days, most of the resistant isolates.

multivariate.note: Only the combining rule is pinned across runtimes. The full scan lives in the desktop because its null shuffles whole isolates so that co-resistance survives, and the portal holds aggregates with no isolate identity in them. Both runtimes must still agree that the combined statistic is the sum of the positive per-stream ratios and nothing else.

process_control.note: Worked examples from the source papers' formulae. No reference package is in wide use for these, so this is a weaker claim than the Farrington validation below and is labelled as one: it proves the two runtimes agree with each other and with the published recursion, not that either agrees with a third implementation.

farrington.note: Validated against R surveillance 1.26.1 algo.farrington, the reference implementation ECDC and UKHSA work from. The counts are a fixed 364-week Poisson series with trend and seasonality and two injected excesses; `reference` is that package's own output at b=5, w=3, alpha=0.01, the 2/3 power transform and limit54=c(5,4). Both AMRIT runtimes reproduce every alarm, every trend decision and every threshold. R indices are 1-based; subtract one.

bayesian.note: Closed-form Gamma-Poisson marginal likelihood, so there is nothing stochastic to pin. The factorial terms that do not depend on the region are omitted throughout, as they cancel in every ratio taken from these values.

external_references.note: Concordance against published, open-source reference implementations that run on every operating system and that a reviewer can install in one command. This replaced the SaTScan round-trip on 14 August 2026: SaTScan is a Windows-first binary that cannot be redistributed, and a concordance claim resting on software a reader must obtain separately is worth less than one they can reproduce. The R packages are not bundled here either — only their output is.

bernoulli.note: Rows flagged `all_cases_inside` are where smerc returns 0 through a 0*log(0) NaN rather than through the statistic being zero. AMRIT takes the limit and returns the finite value, so those rows are excluded from the agreement assertion and asserted separately to be positive. The reference is wrong there and this records which way.

space_time_permutation.note: What is compared is the log-likelihood ratio kernel on identical observed and expected counts. AMRIT's full detector stratifies the expectation by day of week and this reference does not, so a cluster-for-cluster comparison of the two would measure the stratification rather than the implementation. Both find the same zone and the same window on this fixture; only the expectation differs, and it differs by design.

pace.description: Phase 31. The rules PACE is made of, pinned across both runtimes: which mechanism an agent belongs to, the counting rule that makes an isolate resistant to three carbapenems one carbapenem-resistant case, the Sidak correction over the two models, the alert threshold that spends a stated budget, and the transmission-plausibility score. The two scans PACE composes are pinned in the scan and bernoulli sections; the portal cannot run either.
